title: Parsing durations with Result
description:
Parse durations such as `1h30m`, `45s` or `2h5m10s` into seconds, with your own error type:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum DurationError {
    Empty,                        // "duration is empty"
    MissingNumber(char),          // "unit 'm' has no number"
    MissingUnit(String),          // "number 12 has no unit"
    UnknownUnit(char),            // "unknown unit 'x'"
    Overflow,                     // "duration is too long"
}

impl std::fmt::Display for DurationError { ... }   // the messages above

fn parse_duration(text: &str) -> Result<u64, DurationError>
fn total(texts: &[&str]) -> Result<u64, DurationError>      // sum of several durations; the first error wins
fn format_duration(seconds: u64) -> String                   // 5410 gives "1h30m10s"; 0 gives "0s"
```

- Units are `d` (days), `h`, `m` and `s`, each after a whole number; parts may come in any order and repeat (`1m1m` is 120). Spaces around the text are ignored.
- Use `checked_mul` and `checked_add` so huge numbers give `Overflow` instead of wrapping; a number too big for `u64` is also `Overflow`.
- `total` must use `?`.
hints: `c.is_ascii_digit()` tells whether a `char` is `'0'` to `'9'`. Collect digits into a `String` until you meet a unit letter; then parse the digits, multiply by the unit's size and add, all with `checked_` arithmetic turned into errors by `ok_or(...)?`.
`impl fmt::Display` with one `write!` per variant gives every error a human message, and `.to_string()` then works for free.
